Anchal Shukla TGT 19.9.25 The Brain Loves Rhythm APS Vrindavan Yojna Mr. Andrew Steele The Power of Rhythm in Learning: Mr. Steel emphasized how rhythm and melody can aid memory retention, improve pronunciation, and increase learner engagement. He demonstrated how the brain's natural affinity for rhythm can be harnessed to make language learning more effective and enjoyable; the workshop highlighted the benefits of using rhymes in language learning, including : Improved phonological awareness, Enhanced vocabulary retention, Increased confidence in pronunciation; various techniques for incorporating music and rhythm into English language instruction, such as: Using song lyrics to teach grammar and vocabulary, Creating rhythmic patterns to practice pronunciation, Developing chants and rap to reinforce language structures; the workshop included hands-on activities, allowing participants to experience firsthand the impact of rhythm and rhyme on language learning. Mr. Steel shared valuable resources and ideas for integrating these techniques into daily teaching practices.
Mariyam Zehra TGT 18-Sep-25 The brain loves rhythm APS Vrindavan Yojna Andrew stele By the end of the workshop, students will be able to: 1. Recognize the role of rhythm in language learning – understand how rhythm, stress, and intonation patterns improve memory and fluency. 2. Enhance listening and speaking skills – use rhythmic exercises, chants, and patterns to practice correct pronunciation and natural speech flow. 3. Develop vocabulary retention – apply rhythm-based activities to remember new words and phrases more effectively. 4. Boost confidence in communication – participate actively in rhythmic speaking and interactive tasks that make learning engaging. 5. Experience joyful learning – realize that rhythm not only aids memory but also makes English practice fun and motivating.
Shweta Srivastava TGT 18.9.25 The Brain Loves Rhythm APS Vrindavan Yojna Mr. Andrew Steele By the end of the workshop, teachers understood how to: Use rhythm and chanting to make learning engaging, memorable, and stress-free. Apply the Experiential Learning Cycle (experience, reflection, understanding, application) in classroom teaching. Integrate songs, actions, and chants for vocabulary, grammar, and pronunciation practice. Utilize Burlington Publisher resources such as animated videos, apps, gamified vocabulary, listening activities, worksheets, test generator, and grammar mind maps to enrich teaching and support student learning.
